snippet.title: 【クマが町に出没】成人男性4人が小熊に重症、、2025年10月 秋田・東成瀬村クマ襲撃事件
snippet.description:
▼ 書籍を出しました
『秋田 クマ襲撃事件 ── 2016-2025 クマは、もう暮らしのすぐ隣にいる』
この動画の事件を含む、秋田で起きたクマ襲撃事件をまとめた一冊です。

Kindle 299円（Kindle Unlimitedなら0円）／紙の本 1,320円
https://www.amazon.co.jp/dp/B0HHKVMJTW

Kindle Unlimited（30日間無料体験）
https://www.amazon.co.jp/kindle-dbs/hz/signup?tag=a120d-22

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

■動画概要

2025年10月24日、秋田県東成瀬村（ひがしなるせむら）で、村役場からおよそ350メートルの集落を1頭のツキノワグマが襲い、4人が次々と重傷を負いました。

軽トラックへの体当たりから始まり、空き地にいた70代の夫婦、悲鳴を聞いて駆けつけた38歳の男性、そしてその父親へ。わずか数分の出来事でした。

この動画では、複数の一次情報をもとに、地形図とアニメーションで事件の全容を解説します。

現場は、面積の93パーセントを山林と原野が占める、人口2,100人ほどの村。家の勝手口を出て数十歩あるけば山、という環境でした。

駆けつけた消防が4人につけた判定は、全員が「赤」。なぜ4人とも、顔と頭だったのか。

高台からこちらを見下ろすクマに、猟友会は銃口を向けたまま、撃てない時間を過ごします。撃っていいと言えるのは誰なのか。そして、弾はどこへ飛ぶのか。

駆除されたのは、体長1メートル20センチ、体重80キロのメス。決して大きな個体ではありませんでした。

事件の4日前には、隣の湯沢市でも4人が襲われていました。クマは下りてきたのに、情報は下りてこなかった、、

秋田大学の解析が示した「うつ伏せ」という分かれ道、県の要請で入った自衛隊、そして2025年に事件が相次いだ理由であるブナの凶作まで、地形図とアニメーションで解説します。

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
目次
━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

0:00 2025年10月24日、秋田県東成瀬村
0:42 山林が93パーセントの村
1:05 午前10時10分、軽トラックへの体当たり
2:34 午前11時ごろ、住宅の裏手の空き地
3:24 70メートル先の家
4:01 「逃げろ」
4:39 3人目、そして4人目
5:33 4人全員が「赤」
7:29 なぜ、4人とも顔と頭だったのか
8:46 高台から、見下ろしていた
10:13 撃てない時間
12:18 発砲
13:12 体重80キロのメス
14:29 午後4時20分
15:33 4日前の湯沢市
20:23 クマは下りてきた。情報は下りてこなかった
22:45 「うつ伏せ」という、たった一つの分かれ道

26:38 なぜ、2025年だったのか
27:51 そして、半年後

snippet.title: 【クマが町に出没】成人男性4人が小熊に重症、、2025年10月 秋田・東成瀬村クマ襲撃事件
snippet.description:
▼ 書籍を出しました
『秋田 クマ襲撃事件 ── 2016-2025 クマは、もう暮らしのすぐ隣にいる』
この動画の事件を含む、秋田で起きたクマ襲撃事件をまとめた一冊です。

Kindle 299円（Kindle Unlimitedなら0円）／紙の本 1,320円
https://link.amazon/B05HZc0AN

Kindle Unlimited（30日間無料体験）

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

■動画概要

2025年10月24日、秋田県東成瀬村（ひがしなるせむら）で、村役場からおよそ350メートルの集落を1頭のツキノワグマが襲い、4人が次々と重傷を負いました。

軽トラックへの体当たりから始まり、空き地にいた70代の夫婦、悲鳴を聞いて駆けつけた38歳の男性、そしてその父親へ。わずか数分の出来事でした。

この動画では、複数の一次情報をもとに、地形図とアニメーションで事件の全容を解説します。

現場は、面積の93パーセントを山林と原野が占める、人口2,100人ほどの村。家の勝手口を出て数十歩あるけば山、という環境でした。

駆けつけた消防が4人につけた判定は、全員が「赤」。なぜ4人とも、顔と頭だったのか。

高台からこちらを見下ろすクマに、猟友会は銃口を向けたまま、撃てない時間を過ごします。撃っていいと言えるのは誰なのか。そして、弾はどこへ飛ぶのか。

駆除されたのは、体長1メートル20センチ、体重80キロのメス。決して大きな個体ではありませんでした。

事件の4日前には、隣の湯沢市でも4人が襲われていました。クマは下りてきたのに、情報は下りてこなかった、、

秋田大学の解析が示した「うつ伏せ」という分かれ道、県の要請で入った自衛隊、そして2025年に事件が相次いだ理由であるブナの凶作まで、地形図とアニメーションで解説します。

snippet.description:
▼ 書籍を出しました

https://youtu.be/P6129_NW2Zk


■動画概要

2023年5月14日、北海道・幌加内町（ほろかないちょう）の朱鞠内湖（しゅまりないこ）で、釣り人がヒグマに襲われる事件が起きました。

たった一頭のヒグマが、日本最大級の人造湖を丸ごと封鎖してしまいます。
この動画では、複数の一次情報をもとに、地形図とアニメで事件の全容を解説します。

幻の魚イトウが釣れる聖地として知られる朱鞠内湖。事件の5日前、人を恐れないヒグマが目撃され、渡し船による上陸は中止されていました。

しかし、産卵期という最盛期の事情もあり、5日後の5月14日、釣りは再開されます。

10年通う常連だった54歳の男性は、船着き場からおよそ6キロ離れた湖の最奥、ナマコ沢の岸に、たった一人で降り立ちました。

午前10時半、迎えの船が見たのは、男性の胴長（ウェーダー）をくわえた一頭のヒグマと、点々と続く足跡でした。

湖にいた釣り人は全員が船に回収され、日本最大級の湖から人の姿が消えます。

捜索を阻んだのは、獲物に強く執着するというヒグマの習性。翌日、15人のハンターを中心とした捜索隊が入り、国内で初めてとされる赤外線ドローンが投入されました。

駆除された個体は体長およそ1.5メートル、推定3歳のオス。特別に大きな一頭ではありませんでした。

なぜ、この若いクマは人を恐れなかったのか。岸に捨てられる魚、30年で4倍に増えたヒグマ、そして「鈴を鳴らせば逃げる」という常識の終わり、、

事故のあとに作られた「朱鞠内湖ルール」と、遺されたご家族の言葉まで、地形図とアニメで解説します。

en-US.title: [Attacked by an abnormal grizzly...] The tragic end of a 54-year-old who went fishing alone… 2023...
en-US.description:
Videos featured in the video:
[Mountain Accident] Bear spray couldn't stop it... 4 attacks: Rausu-dake Brown Bear Attack Incident, 2025
https://youtu.be/P6129_NW2Zk
■Video Summary

On May 14, 2023, an incident occurred at Lake Shumarinai in Horokanai Town, Hokkaido, where a fisherman was attacked by a brown bear.

A single brown bear completely blocked off one of Japan's largest artificial lakes.
This video explains the entire incident using topographic maps and animation, based on multiple primary sources.

Lake Shumarinai is known as a sacred place for catching the legendary Ito fish. Five days before the incident, a brown bear that showed no fear of humans was sighted, and landing by ferry was suspended.

However, due to the peak spawning season, fishing resumed on May 14th, five days later. A 54-year-old man, a regular customer for 10 years, disembarked alone at the shore of Namako-zawa, at the innermost part of the lake, about 6 kilometers from the dock.

At 10:30 AM, the waiting boat found a brown bear with the man's waders in its mouth, along with a trail of footprints.

All the fishermen on the lake were taken back to the boat, and the lake, one of Japan's largest, became completely devoid of human presence.

The search was hampered by the brown bear's strong attachment to its prey. The following day, a search party, mainly composed of 15 hunters, entered the area, and what is believed to be the first infrared drone in Japan was deployed.

The bear that was culled was approximately 1.5 meters long, an estimated 3-year-old male. It wasn't a particularly large bear.

Why didn't this young bear fear humans? Fish being dumped on the shore, the brown bear population quadrupling in 30 years, and the end of the common belief that "ringing a bell will scare them away"...

This program explains the "Shumarinai Lake Rules" created after the accident, along with the words of the bereaved family, using topographic maps and animation.

映像内で紹介された動画
【山岳遭難事故】クマスプレーでも止まらない、、4度の襲撃 2025年 羅臼岳ヒグマ襲撃事件
https://youtu.be/P6129_NW2Zk


■動画概要

2023年5月14日、北海道・幌加内町（ほろかないちょう）の朱鞠内湖（しゅまりないこ）で、釣り人がヒグマに襲われる事件が起きました。

たった一頭のヒグマが、日本最大級の人造湖を丸ごと封鎖してしまいます。
この動画では、複数の一次情報をもとに、地形図とアニメで事件の全容を解説します。

幻の魚イトウが釣れる聖地として知られる朱鞠内湖。事件の5日前、人を恐れないヒグマが目撃され、渡し船による上陸は中止されていました。

しかし、産卵期という最盛期の事情もあり、5日後の5月14日、釣りは再開されます。

10年通う常連だった54歳の男性は、船着き場からおよそ6キロ離れた湖の最奥、ナマコ沢の岸に、たった一人で降り立ちました。

午前10時半、迎えの船が見たのは、男性の胴長（ウェーダー）をくわえた一頭のヒグマと、点々と続く足跡でした。

湖にいた釣り人は全員が船に回収され、日本最大級の湖から人の姿が消えます。

捜索を阻んだのは、獲物に強く執着するというヒグマの習性。翌日、15人のハンターを中心とした捜索隊が入り、国内で初めてとされる赤外線ドローンが投入されました。

駆除された個体は体長およそ1.5メートル、推定3歳のオス。特別に大きな一頭ではありませんでした。

なぜ、この若いクマは人を恐れなかったのか。岸に捨てられる魚、30年で4倍に増えたヒグマ、そして「鈴を鳴らせば逃げる」という常識の終わり、、

事故のあとに作られた「朱鞠内湖ルール」と、遺されたご家族の言葉まで、地形図とアニメで解説します。

en-US.title: [Attacked by an abnormal grizzly...] The tragic end of a 54-year-old who went fishing alone… 2023...
en-US.description:
Videos featured in the video:
[Mountain Accident] Bear spray couldn't stop it... 4 attacks: Rausu-dake Brown Bear Attack Incident, 2025
https://youtu.be/P6129_NW2Zk
■Video Summary

On May 14, 2023, an incident occurred at Lake Shumarinai in Horokanai Town, Hokkaido, where a fisherman was attacked by a brown bear.

A single brown bear completely blocked off one of Japan's largest artificial lakes.
This video explains the entire incident using topographic maps and animation, based on multiple primary sources.

Lake Shumarinai is known as a sacred place for catching the legendary Ito fish. Five days before the incident, a brown bear that showed no fear of humans was sighted, and landing by ferry was suspended.

However, due to the peak spawning season, fishing resumed on May 14th, five days later. A 54-year-old man, a regular customer for 10 years, disembarked alone at the shore of Namako-zawa, at the innermost part of the lake, about 6 kilometers from the dock.

At 10:30 AM, the waiting boat found a brown bear with the man's waders in its mouth, along with a trail of footprints.

All the fishermen on the lake were taken back to the boat, and the lake, one of Japan's largest, became completely devoid of human presence.

The search was hampered by the brown bear's strong attachment to its prey. The following day, a search party, mainly composed of 15 hunters, entered the area, and what is believed to be the first infrared drone in Japan was deployed.

The bear that was culled was approximately 1.5 meters long, an estimated 3-year-old male. It wasn't a particularly large bear.

Why didn't this young bear fear humans? Fish being dumped on the shore, the brown bear population quadrupling in 30 years, and the end of the common belief that "ringing a bell will scare them away"...

This program explains the "Shumarinai Lake Rules" created after the accident, along with the words of the bereaved family, using topographic maps and animation.

ja.description:
▼ 書籍を出しました

映像内で紹介された動画
【山岳遭難事故】クマスプレーでも止まらない、、4度の襲撃 2025年 羅臼岳ヒグマ襲撃事件
https://youtu.be/P6129_NW2Zk


■動画概要

2023年5月14日、北海道・幌加内町（ほろかないちょう）の朱鞠内湖（しゅまりないこ）で、釣り人がヒグマに襲われる事件が起きました。

たった一頭のヒグマが、日本最大級の人造湖を丸ごと封鎖してしまいます。
この動画では、複数の一次情報をもとに、地形図とアニメで事件の全容を解説します。

幻の魚イトウが釣れる聖地として知られる朱鞠内湖。事件の5日前、人を恐れないヒグマが目撃され、渡し船による上陸は中止されていました。

しかし、産卵期という最盛期の事情もあり、5日後の5月14日、釣りは再開されます。

10年通う常連だった54歳の男性は、船着き場からおよそ6キロ離れた湖の最奥、ナマコ沢の岸に、たった一人で降り立ちました。

午前10時半、迎えの船が見たのは、男性の胴長（ウェーダー）をくわえた一頭のヒグマと、点々と続く足跡でした。

湖にいた釣り人は全員が船に回収され、日本最大級の湖から人の姿が消えます。

捜索を阻んだのは、獲物に強く執着するというヒグマの習性。翌日、15人のハンターを中心とした捜索隊が入り、国内で初めてとされる赤外線ドローンが投入されました。

駆除された個体は体長およそ1.5メートル、推定3歳のオス。特別に大きな一頭ではありませんでした。

なぜ、この若いクマは人を恐れなかったのか。岸に捨てられる魚、30年で4倍に増えたヒグマ、そして「鈴を鳴らせば逃げる」という常識の終わり、、

事故のあとに作られた「朱鞠内湖ルール」と、遺されたご家族の言葉まで、地形図とアニメで解説します。

1996年、ロシア・カムチャッカ。
「クマと心は通じる」と信じ、生涯銃を持たなかった写真家・星野道夫。
その命を奪ったのは、人間が変えてしまった一頭のヒグマでした。

アラスカの原野を18年撮り続け『旅をする木』で知られた世界的写真家は、なぜ"餌付け"されたヒグマに襲われたのか。クリル湖で起きた事件の経緯、額に赤い傷を持つ加害個体の正体、そして10年後に判明した「Food Conditioned（食物条件付け）」の恐ろしさを、地形図とアニメーションで解説します。

snippet.title: 埋められた22歳の大学生、、ピストルが効かない異常グマとの末路… 2023年 大千軒岳ヒグマ事件
snippet.description:
▼ 書籍を出しました
『秋田 クマ襲撃事件 ── 2016-2025 クマは、もう暮らしのすぐ隣にいる』

Kindle 299円（Kindle Unlimitedなら0円）／紙の本 1,320円
https://www.amazon.co.jp/dp/B0HHKVMJTW

Kindle Unlimited（30日間無料体験）
https://www.amazon.co.jp/kindle-dbs/hz/signup?tag=a120d-22

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

2023年10月、北海道渡島管内 福島町の大千軒岳（だいせんげんだけ）で起きた、ヒグマによる二重襲撃事件。
22歳の北海道大学4年生が単独登山中に消失し、3日後、土と木の枝で覆われた姿で発見されました。

10月31日、捜索の下見に入った消防士3名のうち、船板克志さんが体長約1.7メートルのヒグマに馬乗りにされ、助けに入った大原巧海さんが刃渡り5センチの山菜採取用ナイフでヒグマの喉元を突き立てて撃退。3人とも生還しています。

北海道と道総研は「人を恐れず、積極的に攻撃する極めて異例な行動」と分析。

en-US.title: The 22-Year-Old Student Who Was Buried: The Tragic Fate with an Abnormal Bear That Wouldn't Stop ...
en-US.description:
In October 2023, a double attack by a brown bear occurred on Mt. Daisengen in Fukushima Town, Oshima District, Hokkaido.

A 22-year-old fourth-year student at Hokkaido University disappeared while hiking alone and was found three days later covered in soil and branches.

On October 31st, during a reconnaissance mission for the search, one of three firefighters, Katsushi Funaita, was attacked by a brown bear approximately 1.7 meters long. Takumi Ohara intervened, using a 5-centimeter-long foraging knife to stab the bear in the throat and repel it. All three survived.

Hokkaido Prefecture and the Hokkaido Research Organization analyzed the incident as "an extremely unusual act of a bear that showed no fear of humans and actively attacked."

This video explains the full details of the incident and why the tragedy could not be prevented, based on multiple primary sources, using topographic maps and animation.

Three incidents introduced in the video:
1915: Sankebetsu Brown Bear Incident
https://youtu.be/mlvCbz0DP4Y

1970: Fukuoka University Brown Bear Incident
https://youtu.be/c_kkIsQlFe8

May 20, 2016: Towariyama Bear Attack Incident
https://youtu.be/Ot4G3-EHj5Q

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

2023年10月、北海道渡島管内 福島町の大千軒岳（だいせんげんだけ）で起きた、ヒグマによる二重襲撃事件。
22歳の北海道大学4年生が単独登山中に消失し、3日後、土と木の枝で覆われた姿で発見されました。

10月31日、捜索の下見に入った消防士3名のうち、船板克志さんが体長約1.7メートルのヒグマに馬乗りにされ、助けに入った大原巧海さんが刃渡り5センチの山菜採取用ナイフでヒグマの喉元を突き立てて撃退。3人とも生還しています。

北海道と道総研は「人を恐れず、積極的に攻撃する極めて異例な行動」と分析。

この動画では、複数の一次情報をもとに、地形図とアニメで事件の全容と、なぜ悲劇を防げなかったのかを解説します。

en-US.title: The 22-Year-Old Student Who Was Buried: The Tragic Fate with an Abnormal Bear That Wouldn't Stop ...
en-US.description:
In October 2023, a double attack by a brown bear occurred on Mt. Daisengen in Fukushima Town, Oshima District, Hokkaido.

A 22-year-old fourth-year student at Hokkaido University disappeared while hiking alone and was found three days later covered in soil and branches.

On October 31st, during a reconnaissance mission for the search, one of three firefighters, Katsushi Funaita, was attacked by a brown bear approximately 1.7 meters long. Takumi Ohara intervened, using a 5-centimeter-long foraging knife to stab the bear in the throat and repel it. All three survived.

Hokkaido Prefecture and the Hokkaido Research Organization analyzed the incident as "an extremely unusual act of a bear that showed no fear of humans and actively attacked."

This video explains the full details of the incident and why the tragedy could not be prevented, based on multiple primary sources, using topographic maps and animation.

Three incidents introduced in the video:
1915: Sankebetsu Brown Bear Incident
https://youtu.be/mlvCbz0DP4Y

1970: Fukuoka University Brown Bear Incident
https://youtu.be/c_kkIsQlFe8

May 20, 2016: Towariyama Bear Attack Incident
https://youtu.be/Ot4G3-EHj5Q

snippet.description:
▼ 書籍を出しました
『秋田 クマ襲撃事件 ── 2016-2025 クマは、もう暮らしのすぐ隣にいる』

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

1989年10月8日、北アルプス立山連峰で10人中8人が帰らぬ人となった、中高年大量遭難事故。
紅葉狩りのつもりで3,000メートルの稜線に入った登山者を待っていたのは、体感温度マイナス26度の猛吹雪でした。
生き残ったのは2人だけ。10人の運命を分けたのは、一体何だったのでしょうか。

登ったのは京都と滋賀の税理士を中心とした40〜60代の男女10人。前日には気象庁が「日本海側の山で大荒れ」と警告し、麓の内蔵助山荘のオーナーも「明日は山に入るな」と宿泊客に念を押していました。それでも10人は出発。一ノ越で本格的な吹雪に変わった後も、雄山で標準の倍の時間がかかった後も、誰ひとり「引き返そう」とは口にしませんでした。

中高年登山ブームにおける最初の大量遭難として登山界に衝撃を与え、装備基準と撤退判断の重要性を社会に突きつけた1件を、書籍『ドキュメント気象遭難』（羽根田治）の記述をもとに解説します。

en-US.title: Eight out of ten never returned... The two survivors possessed "something"... The 1989 Tateyama m...
en-US.description:
On October 8, 1989, a mass mountaineering accident occurred in the Tateyama mountain range of the Northern Alps, resulting in the deaths of 8 out of 10 climbers.

The climbers, who had entered the 3,000-meter ridge intending to enjoy the autumn foliage, were met with a fierce blizzard with a perceived temperature of minus 26 degrees Celsius.

Only two survived. What separated the fates of the 10?

The group consisted of 10 men and women in their 40s to 60s, mainly tax accountants from Kyoto and Shiga prefectures. The day before, the Japan Meteorological Agency had warned of "severe weather on the mountains along the Sea of ​​Japan," and the owner of the Kuronosuke Mountain Hut at the foot of the mountain had repeatedly urged guests not to enter the mountains the next day. Nevertheless, the 10 set out. Even after the blizzard intensified at Ichinokoshi, and even after it took twice the usual time to reach Oyama, not a single person suggested turning back.

This article, based on the book "Documentary Weather-Related Mountain Accidents" (by Osamu Haneda), explains a case that shocked the mountaineering world as the first mass casualty during the boom in mountaineering among middle-aged and elderly climbers, and highlighted the importance of equipment standards and the decision to retreat.

snippet.title: 10人中8人が帰らぬ人に、、生き残った2人だけが持っていた"あるもの"、、1989年 立山中高年大量遭難事故
snippet.description:
▼ 書籍を出しました
『秋田 クマ襲撃事件 ── 2016-2025 クマは、もう暮らしのすぐ隣にいる』

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

1989年10月8日、北アルプス立山連峰で10人中8人が帰らぬ人となった、中高年大量遭難事故。
紅葉狩りのつもりで3,000メートルの稜線に入った登山者を待っていたのは、体感温度マイナス26度の猛吹雪でした。
生き残ったのは2人だけ。10人の運命を分けたのは、一体何だったのでしょうか。

登ったのは京都と滋賀の税理士を中心とした40〜60代の男女10人。前日には気象庁が「日本海側の山で大荒れ」と警告し、麓の内蔵助山荘のオーナーも「明日は山に入るな」と宿泊客に念を押していました。それでも10人は出発。一ノ越で本格的な吹雪に変わった後も、雄山で標準の倍の時間がかかった後も、誰ひとり「引き返そう」とは口にしませんでした。

中高年登山ブームにおける最初の大量遭難として登山界に衝撃を与え、装備基準と撤退判断の重要性を社会に突きつけた1件を、書籍『ドキュメント気象遭難』（羽根田治）の記述をもとに解説します。

en-US.title: Eight out of ten never returned... The two survivors possessed "something"... The 1989 Tateyama m...
en-US.description:
On October 8, 1989, a mass mountaineering accident occurred in the Tateyama mountain range of the Northern Alps, resulting in the deaths of 8 out of 10 climbers.

The climbers, who had entered the 3,000-meter ridge intending to enjoy the autumn foliage, were met with a fierce blizzard with a perceived temperature of minus 26 degrees Celsius.

Only two survived. What separated the fates of the 10?

The group consisted of 10 men and women in their 40s to 60s, mainly tax accountants from Kyoto and Shiga prefectures. The day before, the Japan Meteorological Agency had warned of "severe weather on the mountains along the Sea of ​​Japan," and the owner of the Kuronosuke Mountain Hut at the foot of the mountain had repeatedly urged guests not to enter the mountains the next day. Nevertheless, the 10 set out. Even after the blizzard intensified at Ichinokoshi, and even after it took twice the usual time to reach Oyama, not a single person suggested turning back.

This article, based on the book "Documentary Weather-Related Mountain Accidents" (by Osamu Haneda), explains a case that shocked the mountaineering world as the first mass casualty during the boom in mountaineering among middle-aged and elderly climbers, and highlighted the importance of equipment standards and the decision to retreat.

snippet.description:

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

2025年8月、北海道・羅臼岳。
クマスプレーを浴びても止まらないヒグマが、26歳の登山者を襲いました。

友人は素手でヒグマに立ち向かいましたが、成人男性2人の抵抗は通じませんでした。

羅臼岳は標高1,661m、日本百名山のひとつ。世界自然遺産・知床半島に位置し、ヒグマの生息密度が極めて高い山域です。

事件の2週間前から、登山道付近で異常な行動をするヒグマの目撃が相次いでいました。
スプレーを浴びても5分間つきまとう。複数の人間がいても逃げない。

その情報は全て関係機関に届いていました。
それでも、登山道は閉鎖されませんでした。

en-US.title: [Mountain Accident] Bear spray couldn't stop it... 4 attacks: Rausu Mountain brown bear attack in...
en-US.description:
August 2025, Mount Rausu, Hokkaido.

A brown bear, undeterred even after being sprayed with bear spray, attacked a 26-year-old hiker.

His friend confronted the bear with his bare hands, but the resistance of two adult men was ineffective.

Mount Rausu, at an elevation of 1,661m, is one of Japan's 100 Famous Mountains. Located on the Shiretoko Peninsula, a World Natural Heritage site, it is a mountain area with an extremely high density of brown bears.

For two weeks prior to the incident, there had been numerous sightings of a brown bear exhibiting unusual behavior near the hiking trail.

It would linger for five minutes even after being sprayed with bear spray. It wouldn't flee even when multiple people were present.

All of this information had been reported to the relevant authorities.

Despite this, the hiking trail was not closed.

This video explains the full details of the incident and why the tragedy could not be prevented, based on the Shiretoko Foundation's preliminary investigation report and interviews with multiple media outlets, along with a topographic map.

2025年8月、北海道・羅臼岳。
クマスプレーを浴びても止まらないヒグマが、26歳の登山者を襲いました。

友人は素手でヒグマに立ち向かいましたが、成人男性2人の抵抗は通じませんでした。

羅臼岳は標高1,661m、日本百名山のひとつ。世界自然遺産・知床半島に位置し、ヒグマの生息密度が極めて高い山域です。

事件の2週間前から、登山道付近で異常な行動をするヒグマの目撃が相次いでいました。
スプレーを浴びても5分間つきまとう。複数の人間がいても逃げない。

その情報は全て関係機関に届いていました。
それでも、登山道は閉鎖されませんでした。

en-US.title: [Mountain Accident] Bear spray couldn't stop it... 4 attacks: Rausu Mountain brown bear attack in...
en-US.description:
August 2025, Mount Rausu, Hokkaido.

A brown bear, undeterred even after being sprayed with bear spray, attacked a 26-year-old hiker.

His friend confronted the bear with his bare hands, but the resistance of two adult men was ineffective.

Mount Rausu, at an elevation of 1,661m, is one of Japan's 100 Famous Mountains. Located on the Shiretoko Peninsula, a World Natural Heritage site, it is a mountain area with an extremely high density of brown bears.

For two weeks prior to the incident, there had been numerous sightings of a brown bear exhibiting unusual behavior near the hiking trail.

It would linger for five minutes even after being sprayed with bear spray. It wouldn't flee even when multiple people were present.

All of this information had been reported to the relevant authorities.

Despite this, the hiking trail was not closed.

This video explains the full details of the incident and why the tragedy could not be prevented, based on the Shiretoko Foundation's preliminary investigation report and interviews with multiple media outlets, along with a topographic map.

en-US.title: The fate of 11 people who ignored a brown bear warning and entered the mountains... The 1976 Fufu...
en-US.description:
June 1976, Mount Fuppushi, Hokkaido.

Despite a warning of brown bear sightings, 11 people from four families entered the mountain to gather bamboo shoots.

A young brown bear attacked them one after another as they scattered in the bamboo thicket.

Three attacks occurred over six days. Those with companions nearby survived, but those who were alone did not make it back.

This video explains the entire incident chronologically and examines why the warning was ignored and why the damage escalated.

▼ Timestamps

0:00 June 1976, Brown Bear Sighting Warning Issued

0:33 Setting Introduction: Mt. Fuppushi and Chishima Bamboo

1:35 First Attack (June 4th)

4:33 Second Attack (June 5th)

8:13 Warning Issued

9:40 11 People Ignoring the Warning Enter the Mountain (June 9th)

12:14 Noon, 3 People Missing

13:00 Discovery and Survival of Mr. Suzuki

15:22 Discovery of Mr. Tanaka and Mr. Kimura

17:31 Pursuit by Hunters and Police

19:06 Close-Range Simultaneous Shooting

20:02 The Identity of the 2-Year-5-Month-Old Male Bear

23:55 The Outcome of the Incident

25:59 Lessons Learned

▼ References

・"Brown Bear" * **Nature of Hokkaido** by Mitsuaki Kadosaki and Tetsuo Inukai (Hokkaido Shimbunsha)

* **Smart FLASH** (April 8, 2023) by Shigehiro Nakayama

* **Hokkaido Prefectural Government: Records of Brown Bear Attacks**

▼ Caution

The names of the victims appearing in this video are all pseudonyms to protect their privacy.

This video was created using AI animation to recreate the situation and characters as accurately as possible.

en-US.title: The fate of 11 people who ignored a brown bear warning and entered the mountains... The 1976 Fufu...
en-US.description:
June 1976, Mount Fuppushi, Hokkaido.

Despite a warning of brown bear sightings, 11 people from four families entered the mountain to gather bamboo shoots.

A young brown bear attacked them one after another as they scattered in the bamboo thicket.

Three attacks occurred over six days. Those with companions nearby survived, but those who were alone did not make it back.

This video explains the entire incident chronologically and examines why the warning was ignored and why the damage escalated.

▼ Timestamps

0:00 June 1976, Brown Bear Sighting Warning Issued

0:33 Setting Introduction: Mt. Fuppushi and Chishima Bamboo

1:35 First Attack (June 4th)

4:33 Second Attack (June 5th)

8:13 Warning Issued

9:40 11 People Ignoring the Warning Enter the Mountain (June 9th)

12:14 Noon, 3 People Missing

13:00 Discovery and Survival of Mr. Suzuki

15:22 Discovery of Mr. Tanaka and Mr. Kimura

17:31 Pursuit by Hunters and Police

19:06 Close-Range Simultaneous Shooting

20:02 The Identity of the 2-Year-5-Month-Old Male Bear

23:55 The Outcome of the Incident

25:59 Lessons Learned

▼ References

・"Brown Bear" * **Nature of Hokkaido** by Mitsuaki Kadosaki and Tetsuo Inukai (Hokkaido Shimbunsha)

* **Smart FLASH** (April 8, 2023) by Shigehiro Nakayama

* **Hokkaido Prefectural Government: Records of Brown Bear Attacks**

▼ Caution

The names of the victims appearing in this video are all pseudonyms to protect their privacy.

This video was created using AI animation to recreate the situation and characters as accurately as possible.

en-US.title: "Freezing" in 20°C temperatures...the invisible weapon that attacked 172 runners
en-US.description:
On May 22, 2021, 21 of the 172 participants lost their lives at a 100km trail running event held in the Yellow River Stone Forest in Gansu Province, China.

A sudden rainstorm and subzero temperatures hit the mountain course at an altitude of over 2,000m, causing the athletes to succumb to hypothermia one after another.

A GPS rescue signal was sent, but the organizers did not respond.

This video provides a detailed explanation of the entire accident, including topographical maps and animations.

#GansuUltramarathon #YellowHeStoneForest #MountainDisaster #TrailRunning #DisasterDocumentary

en-US.title: "Freezing" in 20°C temperatures...the invisible weapon that attacked 172 runners
en-US.description:
On May 22, 2021, 21 of the 172 participants lost their lives at a 100km trail running event held in the Yellow River Stone Forest in Gansu Province, China.

A sudden rainstorm and subzero temperatures hit the mountain course at an altitude of over 2,000m, causing the athletes to succumb to hypothermia one after another.

A GPS rescue signal was sent, but the organizers did not respond.

This video provides a detailed explanation of the entire accident, including topographical maps and animations.

en-US.description:
This video explains the 1964 Mount Iwaki climbing accident.

This incident serves as a stark reminder that even familiar mountains can transform into completely different places depending on the season.

We hope this video provides some valuable lessons.

We offer our deepest condolences to those who lost their lives.

en-US.title: The 2011 Mt. Iwate mountain disaster: what happens when you climb in flip-flops? [Explanation wit...
en-US.description:
In September 2011, on Mount Iwate (elevation 2,038m), a man who began his climb wearing flip-flops and light clothing slipped and fell near the summit. He died from hypothermia.

This article explains the entire accident, where a single piece of equipment made the difference between life and death, using topographic maps and animation.

Past accidents on Mount Iwate and the dangers of climbing with inadequate equipment are also examined.

▼ 書籍を出しました
『秋田 クマ襲撃事件 ── 2016-2025 クマは、もう暮らしのすぐ隣にいる』

Kindle 299円（Kindle Unlimitedなら0円）／紙の本 1,320円
https://link.amazon/B05HZc0AN

Kindle Unlimited（30日間無料体験）
https://www.amazon.co.jp/kindle-dbs/hz/signup?tag=a120a-22

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

2011年9月、岩手山（標高2,038m）。ビーチサンダルに軽装で登山を始めた男性が、山頂付近で滑落。低体温症により命を落とします。
装備ひとつで生死が分かれた事故の全容を、地形図とアニメーションで解説します。
岩手山で過去に起きた事故や、軽装登山の危険性についても検証しました。

en-US.title: The 2011 Mt. Iwate mountain disaster: what happens when you climb in flip-flops? [Explanation wit...
en-US.description:
In September 2011, on Mount Iwate (elevation 2,038m), a man who began his climb wearing flip-flops and light clothing slipped and fell near the summit. He died from hypothermia.

This article explains the entire accident, where a single piece of equipment made the difference between life and death, using topographic maps and animation.

Past accidents on Mount Iwate and the dangers of climbing with inadequate equipment are also examined.

◼︎Reference materials:
Past mountain accident PDF
https://toyokawa-ac.jp/wp-content/uploads/2023/08/%E9%81%8E%E5%8E%BB%E3%81%AE%E9%81%AD%E9%9B%A3%EF%BC%882011%E5%B9%B49%E6%9C%88%EF%BC%89%E5%B2 %A9%E6%89%8B%E5%B1%B1%E9%81%AD%E9%9B%A3%E2%98%85%E2%98%85.pdf

https://www.sankei.com/article/20210504-XQHGWE2F5RM3ZMVAZ4ONPBLCLI/

snippet.title: お金稼ぎのためタケノコ採りに山奥へ…「人喰いクマ」に襲われ結果…2016年5月20日十和利山熊襲撃事件【地形図とアニメで解説】
snippet.description:
▼ 書籍を出しました
『秋田 クマ襲撃事件 ── 2016-2025 クマは、もう暮らしのすぐ隣にいる』

Kindle 299円（Kindle Unlimitedなら0円）／紙の本 1,320円
https://www.amazon.co.jp/dp/B0HHKVMJTW

Kindle Unlimited（30日間無料体験）
https://www.amazon.co.jp/kindle-dbs/hz/signup?tag=a120d-22

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

2016年5月、秋田県・十和利山。タケノコ採りのために入山した人々が、次々とツキノワグマに襲われました。
4人が死亡、4人が重軽傷。なぜクマは「人を食べる」ほど凶暴化したのか。
事件の全容と、ツキノワグマが人を襲うようになった背景を地形図とアニメーションで解説します。

亡くなった方達に心よりご冥福をお祈りします。

en-US.title: A man heads deep into the mountains to gather bamboo shoots to make money... only to be attacked ...
en-US.description:
In May 2016, on Mount Towari in Akita Prefecture, people who had entered the mountain to gather bamboo shoots were attacked one after another by Asiatic black bears.

Four people died, and four were seriously or lightly injured. Why did the bears become so ferocious that they started "eating people"?

This article explains the full details of the incident and the background behind why Asiatic black bears have started attacking humans, using topographic maps and animation.

We offer our deepest condolences to those who lost their lives.

en-US.title: A misfire awakened a hibernating brown bear... The 1878 Sapporo Okadama Incident, which resulted ...
en-US.description:
This time, we explained the 1878 Sapporo Okadama Incident, a wild animal attack that claimed the lives of four people.
This incident shows how failing to hunt a brown bear can lead to widespread harm.

We hope this video serves as a lesson.
We pray for the repose of the souls of those who lost their lives.

en-US.title: Seven dead... A fetus was pulled out of a pregnant woman's womb... The 1915 "Sankebetsu Brown Bea...
en-US.description:
This time, we discussed the 1915 "Sankebetsu Brown Bear Incident," famously known as the worst animal attack in Japanese history. Since brown bears sometimes live in the mountains, we hope this incident will help people learn about their ecology and provide lessons.

We offer our heartfelt condolences to those who lost their lives.

en-US.title: Seven dead... A fetus was pulled out of a pregnant woman's womb... The 1915 "Sankebetsu Brown Bea...
en-US.description:
This time, we discussed the 1915 "Sankebetsu Brown Bear Incident," famously known as the worst animal attack in Japanese history. Since brown bears sometimes live in the mountains, we hope this incident will help people learn about their ecology and provide lessons.

We offer our heartfelt condolences to those who lost their lives.

en-US.title: The tragic truth behind the 2006 Kumakurayama mountain disaster, written in a diary of a man whos...
en-US.description:
In October 2006, on Mount Kumakura in Saitama Prefecture, a male climber who entered the mountain alone went missing. Only his skull was ever found.

His notebook contained a meticulous record of his events from the time of his disappearance until his death.

This article explains the importance of submitting climbing plans, the risks of solo climbing, and typical patterns of getting lost, using topographic maps and animation.

en-US.title: The tragic truth behind the 2006 Kumakurayama mountain disaster, written in a diary of a man whos...
en-US.description:
In October 2006, on Mount Kumakura in Saitama Prefecture, a male climber who entered the mountain alone went missing. Only his skull was ever found.

His notebook contained a meticulous record of his events from the time of his disappearance until his death.

This article explains the importance of submitting climbing plans, the risks of solo climbing, and typical patterns of getting lost, using topographic maps and animation.

en-US.title: Three out of five people died... The fate of a 20-year-old college student who underestimated a b...
en-US.description:
July 1970, Mount Kamui-Ekuchikaushi in the Hidaka Mountains, Hokkaido.

Five members of the Fukuoka University mountaineering club were attacked by a brown bear for three consecutive nights, resulting in one of the worst bear attacks in Japanese mountaineering history, with three losing their lives.

Why couldn't they escape? This video explains the entire incident using topographic maps and animation.

*Regarding the part in the video where the Hokkai Gakuen students' belongings were stolen by the bear but were still in possession the following day, it is likely because they had left spare belongings inside their tent.

en-US.title: Three out of five people died... The fate of a 20-year-old college student who underestimated a b...
en-US.description:
July 1970, Mount Kamui-Ekuchikaushi in the Hidaka Mountains, Hokkaido.

Five members of the Fukuoka University mountaineering club were attacked by a brown bear for three consecutive nights, resulting in one of the worst bear attacks in Japanese mountaineering history, with three losing their lives.

Why couldn't they escape? This video explains the entire incident using topographic maps and animation.

*Regarding the part in the video where the Hokkai Gakuen students' belongings were stolen by the bear but were still in possession the following day, it is likely because they had left spare belongings inside their tent.

en-US.description:

This is a story-based explanation of the mountaineering accident that occurred on Mt. Kunimidake in August 2022.

The story is based on the traces left behind.
As such, it may differ from the actual situation.

It is in no way intended to insult the victims of the accident or their families.
We sincerely hope that this accident will raise a sense of crisis in each individual and help them enjoy the mountains again.
